title_original: Qui prima non c’era il nulla: Lucia Veronesi racconta il nuovo giardino per la città di Gibellina
editorial_title_zh: 这里此前并非一无所有：露西亚·韦罗内西（Lucia Veronesi）讲述吉贝利纳（Gibellina）的新花园
editorial_excerpt_zh: 从上世纪八十年代一个未曾实现的公园项目出发，一件织物作品与一座地中海花园应运而生，它们重新聚焦于当地的历史，以及重建后的城市与乡村景观之间的关系。文章《这里此前并非一无所有：露西亚…》

estinta）深深打动后，我便渴望与她合作，折服于露西亚在其中展现出的原创性、力量与优雅——她将历史、植物学和语言交织在一起，对灭绝这一主题进行了反思。我十分赞赏并认同她的工作方法，这使她能够将理论研究、调查和社群实践系统化[……]。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "克里斯蒂娜·科斯坦佐（Cristina "“我先说明一下项目标题的由来，它灵感来源于我对风景和微创介入（intervento minimo）的研究。在构思阶段，经过最初的实地考察后，我与景观和园林设计师基娅拉·普拉德尔（Chiara Pradel）进行了交流。在我们一次珍贵的交谈中，基娅拉建议我阅读德国社会学家兼城市规划师卢修斯·布克哈特（Lucius Burckhardt）的作品，他的文章被收录在一本名为《虚假与真实》（Il falso è l’autentico）的美丽书籍中。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "布克哈特与伯纳德·拉叙（Bernard Lassus）同为微创介入理论的创立者。后来，通过地中海景观专家、农学家朱塞佩·巴贝拉（Giuseppe Barbera），我发现布克哈特曾在1981年地震后重建的高潮期，协调过一个名为《吉贝利纳的微创介入》的研讨会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/G-CIAC-Telo-e-Giardino-SISILAB-1050-1024x576.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "露西亚·韦罗内西（Lucia Veronesi），《这里此前并非一无所有》（Qui prima non c’era il nulla），2026年。棉质织物、线与刺绣，295×240 cm。图片来源：Sisilab / 吉贝利纳意大利当代艺术之都", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在专门介绍这个研讨会的章节中，我读到：‘任何用一种景观面貌替代另一种景观面貌的人，都必须意识到这种干预会带来什么损失，又会带来什么收获。景观建筑师那种天真的辩解——‘那里以前什么都没有！’——已不再成立。’我立刻觉得这句话可以作为这个项目的标题。不过，我在‘nothing（nothing/nulla）’这个词前加了定冠词‘Il（the）’，以强调那个‘虚无’实际上是一个以某种事物的存在为前提的缺席。因此，《这里此前并非一无所有》（Qui prima non c’era il nulla）暗示了一种不可忽视的先存之物。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《这里此前并非一无所有》是一个复合项目，由一件织物作品和一个地中海花园组成。其中，花园的显著特征是包含了一句用萨布奇纳（Sabucina）石材制作、绵延达22米长的标语文字“这里此前并非一无所有”（Qui prima non c’era il nulla）。为什么会选择这种材料？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“这行字呼应了整个项目的标题，并被安置在城市中极具象征意义的区域，静卧在洛伦佐宫（Palazzo di Lorenzo）前方的绿地上。洛伦佐宫是弗朗切斯科·威尼斯（Francesco Venezia）于上世纪八十年代在吉贝利纳建造的建筑。这行字被构想为地中海花园不可或缺的一部分，我希望它被种植在道路的另一侧，从那里正对著洛伦佐宫。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "弗朗切斯科·威尼斯的建筑融入了这座城市中同名男爵府邸原貌的残存立面，该府邸在1968年的贝利切（Belice）地震中被毁。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/G-CIAC-piantumazione-Veronesi-SISILAB-1022-1024x576.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "露西亚·韦罗内西（Lucia Veronesi），《这里此前并非一无所有》（Qui prima non c’era il nulla），2026年。萨布奇纳（Sabucina）石刻字，2200 x 85 x 8 cm。种有桑树、角豆树和杏树的地中海花园，占地面积约400平方米。图片来源：Sisilab / 吉贝利纳意大利当代艺术之都", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "弗朗切斯科·威尼斯在其中使用了多种材料，包括萨布奇纳石，这是一种能够抵抗外部侵蚀的本地砂岩。在从概念和技术层面权衡出最佳材料，并使其既能与弗朗切斯科·威尼斯的作品相协调、又能融入西西里风景之后，我的选择便落在了萨布奇纳石上。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这组字被放置在野生植被生长的一片土地上，紧邻一处芦苇荡。顺应季节的更迭，杂草和植物将会部分覆盖这些文字，使其刻意呈现出不易辨认的状态。然而在夏季，这句话又会重新显现。将字母平行于地面安装的选择，使得它们只能从某些特定的视点被观赏，特别是从不远处的孔萨格拉剧院（Teatro di Consagra）内部。这些字母高85厘米、厚8厘米，在草坪上延伸了22米长：我希望它们是一种具象的存在，不会迷失在风景中，但同时又与环境和谐共存、不显得突兀。»,", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/G-CIAC-Telo-e-Giardino-SISILAB-1048-1024x576.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "Lucia Veronesi, Qui prima non c’era il nulla, 2026. 萨布奇纳石镌刻文字，2200 x 85 x 8 cm。种有桑树、角豆树和杏树的地中海花园，占地面积约 400 平方米。鸣谢：Sisilab，为吉贝利纳意大利当代艺术之都（Gibellina capitale italiana dell'arte contemporanea）项目提供支持", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在那片土地上，在朱塞佩·巴尔贝拉的咨询指导下，人们种植了桑树、角豆树和杏树。为什么会选择这些树木？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«我的作品的灵感来源是20世纪80年代由农学家朱塞佩·巴尔贝拉和建筑师皮特罗·布尔佐塔（Pietro Burzotta）为吉贝利纳设计、但从未实现的博物馆花园。他们的方案构想了一座织锦般的网格花园，其灵感来自保罗·克利（Paul Klee）在西西里岛旅行期间创作的地中海风景画之一。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "他们的设计理念成为了我织物作品构思的起点，同时也成了一个宝贵的契机，得以切实打造一座旨在让一处废弃绿地重焕生机的全新花园。正因如此，织物作品与地中海花园互为补充，是一个完整的项目。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在西西里大区制图档案库进行的检索、对巴勒莫植物园标本馆（Erbario dell’Orto Botanico di Palermo）的查阅，以及随后与巴勒莫大学树木栽培学前教授兼农学家朱塞佩·巴尔贝拉展开的对话，对于通过种植桑树、杏树和角豆树来向城市及其社群重现一座地中海乡村花园的决定，起到了至关重要的作用。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/G-CIAC-Telo-e-Giardino-SISILAB-1046-1024x576.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "露西亚·韦罗内西（Lucia Veronesi），《此处以前并非一无所有》（Qui prima non c’era il nulla），2026年。萨布西纳石（pietra di Sabucina）文字雕刻，2200 x 85 x 8厘米。种植了桑树、角豆树和杏树的地中海花园，占地约400平方米。鸣谢：Sisilab，为吉贝利纳意大利当代艺术之都项目", "credit": "Exibart", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "巴尔贝拉坚信，乡村景观不仅应保留实用性，还应兼具美感，而这两者在“花园”这一场域中交汇。事实上，实用与美丽对于农业而言是必不可少的，农业在进行生产的同时，不应破坏景观，而应与其进行和谐的互动。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "请给我们讲讲更多细节", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«我们还探讨了不同花期的交替，以及角豆树作为一种强韧树种的存在，它的树冠向水平方向展开以创造出阴凉区域。用巴尔贝拉的话说，“有树木的地方就有树荫、水源、休憩、花园和家”（引自朱塞佩·巴尔贝拉《地中海花园：从荷马到人类世的故事与景观》（Il giardino del mediterraneo, storie e paesaggi da Omero all’Antropocene），Il Saggiatore出版社，2021年）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些树木是按照三个并排网格的方案进行种植的：中央网格种植角豆树，两侧网格则分别种植杏树和桑树，以此在理念上呼应巴尔贝拉和布尔佐塔的项目以及保罗·克利的绘画。»,", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://www.exibart.com/repository/media/2026/10/G-CIAC-Telo-e-Giardino-SISILAB-1021-819x1024.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "露西亚·韦罗内西（Lucia Veronesi），《此处以前并非一无所有》（Qui prima non Corrao）非常珍视的主题。作为吉贝利纳地震后重建阶段的主导人物，这位具有远见的市长极力支持旨在恢复景观（作为乡村、经济、社会和文化现实）的项目。科拉奥规划的重建不仅涉及房屋和城市，还包括花园和乡村——这是贝利切河谷的独特特质，也是同一进程的一部分。当时需要缝合城市与乡村的织体，但正如科拉奥本人在朱塞佩·拉·莫尼卡（Giuseppe La Monica）的书《吉贝利纳：意识形态与乌托邦》（Gibellina, Ideologia e utopia，雷安·马佐内（Rean Mazzone）与玛丽亚·穆拉斯（Maria Mulas）摄影，伦佐·马佐内出版社（Renzo Mazzone Editore），1981年）中所写的那样，这一愿景由于缺乏资金和意愿而未能实现».", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "预计会是怎样的一种观赏体验？这片土地上会设有座椅吗？可以踩踏吗？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«我们没有选择带有步道和长椅的装饰性设计花园；相反，我们设想了一座更接近“小树林”概念、可供人体验的地中海花园。这座新花园将沿着孔萨格拉剧院生长，在一片亟待活化、且本已存在芦苇荡和地中海灌木林的区域创造出一片阴凉区。»,", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "«织物与地中海花园是同一项目的不同表达，这也是它们共享同一个标题的原因。这是一项集体创作，建立在与社群及当地的持续交流基础之上，是我通过多次实地考察和一段漫长的驻留期最终酝酿成熟的。在6月至7月期间，我通过缝纫机制作了一件大型棉质织物（295 x 240厘米）：我选择了让人联想起贝利切河谷景观的颜色，包括黄色、绿色和大地色。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我重新整理了巴勒莫植物园标本馆关于吉贝利纳及周边地区植物物种的数据。织物上交织并堆叠着受这些植物（如灌木紫罗兰、海苜蓿、刺山柑、粉花葱和岩紫草）启发的碎片化形态，它们以一种新的笔触唤起人们对地中海花园的想象。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": Sarà grazie a chi abita quel territorio che il lavoro continuerà a crescere»."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "I nfine, in definitiva, qual è il pensiero dell’opera?"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "«Attraverso il giardino e il tessuto l’opera si fa metafora di riflessione su ciò che c’era prima della ricostruzione post-terremoto, riattivando un paesaggio, citando Giuseppe Barbera, che è fatto di cultura, coltura e cura. Gibellina non è un luogo qualsiasi, è un luogo mitico, con le sue contraddizioni, le sue utopie e i suoi fallimenti. Inserirsi in un tessuto urbano, sociale, naturale come questo ha rappresentato una grande sfida, ha comportato tempo e costanza che sono serviti a lasciarmi attraversare da questo territorio: l’unico modo per poter restituire una visione più intima e personale rimanendo fedeli alla storia che questo paesaggio ci racconta»."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Conclude Costanzo «Al patrimonio storico-artistico di Gibellina si aggiunge così una nuova opera, capace di dialogare non soltanto con Palazzo Di Lorenzo e il Teatro di Consagra ma con l’idea più ampia di spazio della collettività. «Il mio incontro con Lucia Veronesi è avvenuto nel solco del comune interesse per il ricorso al tessuto nelle arti visive e per l’attenzione verso il mondo della natura e la botanica nelle intersezioni con l’arte al femminile. Ho desiderato lavorare con lei dopo essere rimasta particolarmente colpita dal suo progetto La desinenza estinta , per l’originalità, la forza e la grazia con cui Lucia ha riflettuto sul tema dell’estinzione intrecciando storia, botanica e linguaggio. Apprezzo e condivido il suo metodo di lavoro che le consente di mettere a sistema studi teorici, ricerca e pratiche comunitarie […]».

Così Cristina Costanzo , curatrice del progetto Qui prima non c’era il nulla di Veronesi per Gibellina Capitale Italiana dell’Arte Contemporanea 2026 , introduce l’artista che «riesce a riflettere su una questione nodale nella storia di Gibellina e cioè il rapporto con lo spazio pubblico e con lo spazio della natura in relazione alla comunità».

Abbiamo parlato con Lucia Veronesi per approfondire il progetto gibellinese Qui prima non c’era il nulla .

Lucia Veronesi , come avviene l’approdo a Gibellina?

«Nel 2024 sono stata invitata da Cristina Costanzo a proporre un progetto per la candidatura di Gibellina Capitale dell’Arte Contemporanea 2026 a partire da una riflessione sul paesaggio, coerentemente con la mia ricerca.

Conoscevo già quei luoghi e il Cretto di Burri ma questo progetto è stato l’inizio di una lunga avventura e di un bellissimo sodalizio professionale e umano con Cristina, che ha seguito e curato il progetto fin dalle prime fasi, con molta attenzione e passione».

La doppia negazione del titolo Qui prima non c’era il nulla cosa comporta?

«Faccio una premessa sull’origine del titolo del progetto, ispirato dalle mie ricerche sul paesaggio e l’intervento minimo. Mentre lavoravo alle fasi di ideazione, dopo i primi sopralluoghi, mi sono confrontata con Chiara Pradel , un’architetta che si occupa di paesaggio e giardini. Durante una delle nostre preziose chiacchierate, Chiara mi suggerisce di leggere Lucius Burckhardt , sociologo e urbanista tedesco, i cui testi sono raccolti in un bellissimo libro, Il falso è l’autentico .

Burckhardt è, insieme a Bernard Lassus , autore della teoria dell’intervento minimo. Scopro poi, grazie a Giuseppe Barbera , agronomo esperto di paesaggio mediterraneo, che Burckhardt nel 1981 aveva coordinato un seminario dal titolo L’intervento minimo a Gibellina, nel pieno della ricostruzione post-terremoto.

Nel capitolo dedicato a questo seminario leggo “ Chi sostituisce un aspetto del paesaggio con un altro deve rendersi conto di cosa si perde e di cosa si guadagna con un simile intervento. La candida difesa dell’architetto del paesaggio – lì prima non c’era nulla! – non è più ammissibile ”. Penso subito che questa espressione possa diventare il titolo del progetto. Aggiungo però l’articolo “Il” davanti alla parola “nulla” enfatizzando l’idea che quel nulla è un’assenza che presuppone la presenza di qualcosa. Qui prima non c’era il nulla indica quindi un preesistente che non si può ignorare».

Qui prima non c’era il nulla è un progetto composito che si articola in un’opera tessile e un giardino mediterraneo. Il giardino, in particolare, è connotato dalla presenza della scritta Qui prima non c’era il nulla , realizzata in pietra di Sabucina e che si estende per 22 metri di lunghezza. Come mai la scelta di questo materiale?

«La scritta riprende il titolo dell’intero progetto e si colloca in un’area altamente simbolica della città, adagiandosi nell’area verde antistante Palazzo di Lorenzo, edificio realizzato da Francesco Venezia a Gibellina negli anni Ottanta. La scritta è concepita come parte integrante del giardino mediterraneo, che ho voluto che venisse piantato al di là della strada, da dove guarda Palazzo di Lorenzo.

L’architettura di Francesco Venezia incorpora quel che rimane della facciata originale dell’omonimo palazzo baronale della città vecchia, distrutto dal terremoto del Belice del 1968.

Francesco Venezia vi utilizza diversi tipi di materiali, tra cui la Sabucina, una pietra arenaria locale resistente agli agenti esterni. Ragionando sul materiale migliore, sia a livello concettuale sia a livello tecnico, e che fosse in armonia tanto con l’opera di Francesco Venezia quanto con il paesaggio siciliano la mia scelta è ricaduta quindi sulla pietra di Sabucina.

La scritta è stata posata su un terreno dove cresce una vegetazione spontanea, accanto a un canneto. Assecondando i ritmi delle stagioni, l’erba e le piante ricopriranno in parte la scritta che, intenzionalmente, sarà poco leggibile. Con la stagione estiva, invece, la frase sarà di nuovo visibile. La scelta di installare le lettere parallelamente al suolo le rende fruibili solo da alcuni punti di vista, in particolare dall’interno del Teatro di Consagra, poco distante. Le lettere misurano 85 cm di altezza per 8 cm di spessore e si sviluppano sul prato per una lunghezza di 22 metri: volevo che fossero una presenza concreta, che non si perdessero nel paesaggio ma che al tempo stesso fossero armoniche e non invasive».

Su quel terreno, con la consulenza di Giuseppe Barbera, sono stati piantati gelsi, carrubi e mandorli. Perché la scelta di questi alberi?

«La fonte di ispirazione della mia opera è un giardino museo progettato, ma mai realizzato, per Gibellina negli anni Ottanta dall’agronomo Giuseppe Barbera e dall’architetto Pietro Burzotta . Il loro progetto prevedeva un giardino a tessere, ispirato a uno dei dipinti dei paesaggi mediterranei che Paul Klee ha realizzato durante un viaggio in Sicilia.

La loro idea progettuale è stata il punto di partenza per l’ideazione della mia opera in tessuto, ma si è rivelata anche una preziosa occasione per dare vita, concretamente, a un nuovo giardino destinato a riqualificare un’area verde abbandonata. È per questa ragione che l’opera in tessuto e il giardino mediterraneo, complementari tra loro, sono un progetto unico.

Le ricerche presso l’archivio cartografico della Regione Sicilia, la consultazione dell’Erbario dell’Orto Botanico di Palermo e successivamente il dialogo sviluppato con Giuseppe Barbera, agronomo e già docente di Colture arboree nell’Università di Palermo, sono stati fondamentali per la scelta di restituire alla città e alla sua comunità un giardino rurale mediterraneo attraverso la presenza di alberi di gelsi, mandorli e carrubi.

Barbera è sostenitore dell’idea che il paesaggio rurale debba preservare l’utilità ma anche la bellezza e che essi si incontrano nel luogo “giardino”. L’utile e il bello, infatti, sono necessari all’agricoltura, che oltre a produrre, non deve danneggiare il paesaggio ma interagire con esso in maniera armonica.

Dicci di più

«Si è ragionato anche sull’alternarsi delle fioriture e sul carrubo, come presenza di albero resistente, con una chioma che si espande in orizzontale per creare zone d’ombra. Per citare Barbera “dove ci sono gli alberi c’è l’ombra, l’acqua, il riposo, il giardino e la casa” (Giuseppe Barbera, Il giardino del mediterraneo, storie e paesaggi da Omero all’Antropocene. Ed. Il Saggiatore, 2021).

Gli alberi sono stati piantati secondo uno schema di tre tessere affiancate, quella centrale con i carrubi e le laterali con mandorli e gelsi ai lati, per riallacciarsi idealmente al progetto di Barbera e Burzotta e alla pittura di Paul Klee».

La relazione tra la ricostruzione della città e la campagna è stata un tema molto caro a Ludovico Corrao , il sindaco visionario, protagonista della fase post-simica di Gibellina e sostenitore di progetti volti al recupero del paesaggio, quale realtà rurale, economica, sociale e culturale. Corrao progettava una ricostruzione che doveva riguardare sì la casa e la città ma anche il giardino e la campagna, caratteristica peculiare della valle del Belice, nonché parte dello stesso processo. Bisognava ricucire il tessuto città-campagna, ma per questa visione sono mancati i finanziamenti e la volontà, come scrive lo stesso Corrao nel libro di Giuseppe La Monica , Gibellina, Ideologia e Utopia (Giuseppe La Monica, Gibellina, Ideologia e utopia. Foto di Rean Mazzone e Maria Mulas. Renzo Mazzone Editore, 1981)».

C he tipo di fruizione è prevista? Il terreno prevede delle sedute? È calpestabile?

«La scelta non è ricaduta su un giardino ornamentale e disegnato, con camminamenti e panchine; si è pensato invece a un giardino mediterraneo che fosse più vicino a un’idea di “boschetto” da fruire. Il nuovo giardino crescerà di fianco al teatro di Consagra e creerà una zona d’ombra in un’area da valorizzare e dove erano già presenti canneti e una macchia mediterranea».

C ome nasce – ad affiancamento, ma completamente indipendente – la grande opera in tessuto omonima realizzata con le ricamatrici gibellinesi del laboratorio Artensis, fondato da Antonella Corrao? Come si rapportano le due opere?

«Il tessuto e il giardino mediterraneo sono espressione dello stesso progetto ed è questo il motivo per cui condividono il medesimo titolo. Si tratta di un lavoro corale, supportato dal continuo scambio con la comunità e con il territorio, che ho maturato grazie a numerosi sopralluoghi e una lunga residenza. Tra giugno e luglio ho realizzato, cucendo a macchina, un grande tessuto in cotone (295 x 240 cm): ho scelto i colori che richiamano il paesaggio della valle del Belice, i gialli, i verdi e le terre.

Ho rielaborato i dati desunti dall’Erbario dell’Orto Botanico di Palermo sulle specie vegetali che si trovano nell’area di Gibellina e nelle zone limitrofe. Sul tessuto si incrociano e si accumulano forme frammentate ispirate a queste piante (come la violaciocca cespugliosa, l’erba medica marina, l’erba barba, l’aglio roseo e l’alcanna), che evocano un giardino mediterraneo ma in una nuova scrittura.

Ho poi affidato il tessuto alle bravissime ricamatrici del Laboratorio Artensis, fondato da Antonella Corrao , che hanno sapientemente ricamato la scritta Qui prima non c’era il nulla , coadiuvate dalla maestra ricamatrice Maria Mercante.

Dove verrà conservata l’opera?

La scelta del punto, dopo confronti e prove è ricaduta sul punto erba, accostato e riempitivo, con un filato cangiante che non ricopre tutta la superficie delle lettere ma si confonde, volutamente, a tratti, con i colori di base del tessuto e dona riflessi, variazioni di luce, matericità, esaltando i differenti spessori dei tessuti. Questo mimetismo, in particolare, è uno degli aspetti che connettono l’opera in tessuto e il giardino.

Il progetto Qui prima non c’era il nulla verrà presentato durante un incontro pubblico e l’opera in tessuto sarà collocata all’interno di Palazzo di Lorenzo per riallacciarsi a un percorso coerente con il giardino sottostante e arricchirà il patrimonio storico-artistico della città».

C ome avviene la stratificazione di questo progetto?

« Qui prima non c’era il nulla è un progetto complesso le cui parti sono connesse e complementari e si basano sulla ricerca di un equilibrio, estetico e concettuale, che si destreggia tra piani e livelli, sovrapposizioni e stratificazioni.

Il progetto stabilisce un dialogo con il territorio e con chi questo territorio lo abita.

È un lavoro che incrocia diverse discipline, che ha visto molti sopralluoghi e molta ricerca per «comprendere al meglio un luogo per me mitico ed estremamente affascinante, ma anche lontano dalle mie origini. È un’opera corale fatta di continui scambi e confronti a partire dal dialogo con Cristina Costanzo, ma anche con i tecnici del comune, i giardinieri, gli scout. Mi sono messa in ascolto del territorio, con curiosità e rispetto, e il risultato finale è un progetto che richiede comunque cure e attenzioni anche dopo la sua presentazione ufficiale. Sarà grazie a chi abita quel territorio che il lavoro continuerà a crescere».

I nfine, in definitiva, qual è il pensiero dell’opera?

«Attraverso il giardino e il tessuto l’opera si fa metafora di riflessione su ciò che c’era prima della ricostruzione post-terremoto, riattivando un paesaggio, citando Giuseppe Barbera, che è fatto di cultura, coltura e cura. Gibellina rinasce su un territorio dove non c’era “il nulla”, ma anzi dove già convivevano storie e relazioni intrecciate alla terra e al paesaggio.

Mi sono sentita investita di una grande responsabilità quando Cristina mi ha chiesto di pensare a un progetto per la città; responsabilità che è diventata ancora più grande quando si è concretizzata la realizzazione di un’opera permanente. Gibellina non è un luogo qualsiasi, è un luogo mitico, con le sue contraddizioni, le sue utopie e i suoi fallimenti. Inserirsi in un tessuto urbano, sociale, naturale come questo ha rappresentato una grande sfida, ha comportato tempo e costanza che sono serviti a lasciarmi attraversare da questo territorio: l’unico modo per poter restituire una visione più intima e personale rimanendo fedeli alla storia che questo paesaggio ci racconta».

Conclude Costanzo «Al patrimonio storico-artistico di Gibellina si aggiunge così una nuova opera, capace di dialogare non soltanto con Palazzo Di Lorenzo e il Teatro di Consagra ma con l’idea più ampia di spazio della collettività. Sono felice che questo nuovo intervento, che rifiuta il monumentalismo in nome di una sinergia con il paesaggio e si fa pratica di ascolto sviluppandosi rasoterra e orizzontalmente, quasi a mimetizzarsi con la natura, sia stato realizzato da un’artista donna proprio in un luogo che ha accolto le ricerche di artiste straordinarie come Carla Accardi e Nanda Vigo ».

article_text:
Das Haus am Waldsee, das Kunsthaus Dahlem, das Georg Kolbe Museum und das Brücke-Museum erinnern mit der Aktion an den kostenlosen Museumssonntag. Sie bieten Führungen, Workshops und andere Aktionen

Freier Eintritt in vier Berliner Museen: Das Haus am Waldsee, das Kunsthaus Dahlem, das Georg Kolbe Museum und das Brücke-Museum laden für den heutigen Sonntag zu einem kostenlosen Besuch ein. Es gebe verschiedene Aktionen und Workshops, teilten die Museen mit.

Im Georg Kolbe Museum ist der Eintritt zur neuen Ausstellung "everybody" frei. Im Kunsthaus Dahlem liest unter anderem die Autorin Anna Shapiro aus ihrem Buch "Fühlen Sie sich wie zu Hause, aber vergessen Sie dabei nicht, dass Sie zu Gast sind". Außerdem gibt es einen Workshop zur Porträtgestaltung.

Das Haus am Waldsee gibt eine Führung durch die Ausstellung und einen Drop-In-Workshop zum Thema "Ein Haus – viele Bilder". Im Brücke-Museum gibt es einen Rundgang zu der Rolle von Landschaften in den Arbeiten der Brücke-Künstler durch die Ausstellungen "Draußen ... im Museum" und "Draußen unter Kiefern".

Erinnerung an kostenlosen Museumssonntag

Die Häuser wollen damit ein Zeichen für einen offenen und niedrigschwelligen Zugang zu Kunst und Kultur setzen, und an den kostenlosen Berliner Museumssonntag anknüpfen, an dem früher einmal im Monat der Eintritt in die Berliner Museen frei war. Möglich sei die heutige Aktion durch eine großzügige Spende, hieß es.

Der Zeitpunkt sei bewusst gewählt: Während der Koalitionsgespräche zur Bildung eines neuen Senats stehen Haushaltsentscheidungen an, und damit auch kulturpolitische Schwerpunkte, hieß es. Die Wiedereinführung des kostenlosen Museumssonntags war parteiübergreifend in die Wahlprogramme aufgenommen worden.

To receive Morning Links in your inbox every weekday, sign up for our Breakfast with ARTnews newsletter.

Good morning!

The Louvre, Musée d’Orsay, Picasso Museum and the Grand Palais’ exhibition spaces will all close on Saturday in anticipation of planned protests in the French capital.

Artist duo Brognon Rollin (David Brognon and Stéphanie Rollin) just won the Marcel Duchamp Prize.

Nearly 1,000 objects from the family of former Spanish dictator Francisco Franco have seen their value explode ahead of a sale at Magna Art Auctions, but historic preservationist groups want to stop the sale.

The Headlines

PARIS MUSEUMS GO MUM. The Louvre, Musée d’Orsay, Picasso Museum and the Grand Palais ’ exhibition spaces will all close on Saturday in anticipation of planned protests in the French capital, reports Le Figaro . The French Ministry of Culture urged all national and public museums to do everything necessary to ensure the safety and security of visitors, workers, and artworks. Many shops have started boarding up their windows in case of a second round of looting, following last weekend’s civil unrest in the wake of mostly peaceful protests about social and economic inequality amid a rising cost of living, held across France. In an attempt to maintain order, French President Emmanuel Macron announced that only protests organized by unions are authorized on Saturday, and partial curfews will be put in place in several cities. He blamed last weekend’s violence on “political and seditious acts by the ultra-far-left groups who aimed to bring down the republic.”

DUCHAMP PRIZE IS (AL)READYMADE. Artist duo Brognon Rollin ( David Brognon and Stéphanie Rollin) just won the Marcel Duchamp Prize in Paris for their project “5,376 years, 1892 months, 1110 days, 1201 hours,” announced the Musée d’Art Moderne de Paris (MAM) . For their winning project, the duo, who live and work between Paris and Luxembourg, collected sobriety tokens from members of abstinence groups, which represent the amount of time a person has been sober. They then added up the time they collectively represented and displayed them in an installation evocative of arcade or fairground games. “With Brognon Rollin, the Marcel Duchamp Prize recognizes a demanding body of work that is committed to materializing what usually escapes the eye: the time of waiting, of addiction, and of intimate resistance,” said Fabrice Hergott , director of MAM.

The Digest

Everyday items and mementos from the family of former Spanish dictator Francisco Franco have seen their value explode ahead of a sale at Magna Art Auctions later this month , but historic preservationist groups claim many of the lots include items of national heritage, and they want to suspend the sale. [ El Pais ]

A man was arrested for using a sledgehammer to behead the figure of a Marine depicted in the Iwo Jima statue, in Quantico, Virginia, causing hundreds of thousands of dollars in damage. [ NBC Washington ]

A March-introduced legislative bill could significantly expand the French government’s definition of art considered a “national treasure,” which requires export certificates that may be refused. [ The Art Newspaper ]

Los Angeles architects Johnston Marklee have released design plans for the expansion of the Bass Museum of Art in Miami Beach. [ Artforum ]

The forthcoming Róng Museum of Art (RMoA) in Shenzhen has appointed three new members to its curatorial team ahead of its 2027 opening: Freya Chou, Li Jia , and Susanna Zhu . [ ArtAsiaPacific ]

The Kicker

FIRST STAR I SEE TONIGHT, WISH I MAY… Researchers believe they have cracked the science behind Vincent van Gogh ’s iconic painting, The Starry Night (1889), reports the Times of London . They think those famous swirls he depicted in the star-lit sky actually show the Taurus constellation, marked by a waning crescent moon, the planet Venus, and the Hyades star cluster. Given that the Dutch artist was known to look out the east window of his room in an asylum in the village of Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, and using a technique for superimposing images of the stars at that moment on top of the painting, scientists believe he was inspired by the landscape and sky he saw on July 22, 1889, to be exact. That date is a month later than previously estimated, and it also shows Van Gogh’s method of painting from observation. “It has been debated whether the night sky in question was the painter’s fantasy, a symbolic representation, or a realistic astronomical observation,” said the Springer Nature group, which publishes the Scientific Reports journal.

article_text:
I n case you were somehow blissfully unaware, America is in a very dark place and Americans are not very happy about it. Last week’s midterms saw a historic blue wave propelled by the high cost of living and the low trust in those making decisions, but restoring any small shred of faith in the system and any vague semblance of financial equity is still unlikely to come any time soon.

It’s therefore theoretically ideal timing for films that provide some sort of rousing David v Goliath catharsis, a win on-screen when one feels entirely out of reach in real life. But like Paul Greengrass’s muddy and muddled peasant revolt drama The Uprising which crashed and burned in September, David Leitch’s How to Rob a Bank can’t quite find a way to capture a moment that should be easy to capture. The director is best known for synthetic action films that prioritise noise above all else, from Deadpool 2 to Bullet Train to Hobbs & Shaw, a tonal through-line that could be most generously described as “annoying”.

He’s operating in a slightly less frenetic mode here (radically, people stop and sit down to talk in a number of scenes) but for a film that’s supposed to enrage and excite and energise, it’s all strangely, boringly flat and with a runtime just stretching past two hours, surprisingly sluggish too. It’s a shame as there’s an effectively startling premise that does initially grab: a group of masked criminals are playing both bank robbers and online activists by pulling off heists and telling their followers how to do the same. They’re also playing Robin Hood by donating portions of their haul to local charities that need it the most.

The team is populated by Pittsburgh locals who have legitimate reasons to want to push back and rise up, all suffering from a “common pain”, maddened by healthcare costs, immigration enforcement, military mistreatment and, naturally, predatory banks. Their leader is Ryan (a visibly bored Nicholas Hoult) who is joined by his partner, Emi (Shogun breakout Anna Sawai, given depressingly little to say or do) and friends Vince (Pete Davidson) and Hugo (Rhenzy Feliz). As their virality expands, an exhausted FBI agent “five years away from retirement” (John C Reilly) enlists a dubious house-arrested hacker (Zoë Kravitz) to take them down.

Like many a film focused so intently on the power of the internet, How to Rob a Bank was always going to feel almost instantly dated. Very few films about how we live digitally have managed this well (Ingrid Goes West remains an impressive outlier) but even taking this into consideration and allowing for certain shifts, there’s something rather embarrassing here about what’s viewed as current. The videos that are put out by the team would have felt passé a decade ago, a chintzy lolcat visual style that never once feels like anything but something a man made in his 50s would consider cutting edge. It doesn’t help that the film also arrives after a summer of gen Z hits made by actual gen Z film-makers who know how to appeal with authenticity and one feels that getting someone in the room who actually understands what goes viral in 2026 would have been greatly beneficial. We barely get to hear much from the robbers for the most part, which might be a relief given how much we get to hear from Kravitz’s creaky stoner stereotype. The actor, playing a dumbed down CBS sitcom riff on her Kimi character, arrives on-screen with a Cheeto in her hair (!) and it somehow gets worse from there – her quirks being that she “really likes good coffee” and just can’t stop snacking or getting advice from her chatbot. The soundtrack is similarly out-of-step with The Hives’s Tick Tick Boom and Lily Allen’s Fuck You making one question just when the film is supposed to be set.

So for a film all about reflecting this awful moment that we’re in, it never really feels like we’re in this awful moment, just a loose idea of what it looks like from afar. Merely pointing at obvious targets does not count as social commentary, and while screenwriter Mark Bianculli does arguably have his heart in the right place (billionaires sure are bad!), it’s a little hard to stomach an anti-capitalism screed not only funded by Amazon but featuring several scenes of lame, please-aim-logo-towards-camera, product placement (after one dismantles the system, a refreshing can of Mountain Dew really does hit the spot). The film wants to present as anarchic but it’s as counter-culture and behind the times as an Occupy Wall Street bumper sticker on an SUV, a point most directly made when Reilly’s FBI agent tells us that in all of this, it’s actually the cops we should be pitying the most, just not the racist ones. OK, sure dad.

Its playschool politics might have been somewhat tolerated had there been much else here to enjoy, but the heist sequences are both smugly framed yet dimly thought through and there’s never any remote emotional attachment to the group or real burning anger for what they are fighting for. Set It Off, a searing 1996 heist movie about four beaten down women taking charge, still carries more urgency and power in one scene than this does in the entire duration (Bianculli even cheekily lifts a shootout death from that film yet it carries over none of the impact). As the inevitable high-stakes last heist rears its head and as masked “anarchy” grips the streets of Pittsburgh, you’ll be hard pressed to cheer any of it on. Fighting against the system can sure feel hopeless at times but it really shouldn’t feel this pointless.

How to Rob a Bank is in Australian cinemas on 12 November and in the US and UK on 13 November

title_original: « L’Âge d’or » de Bérenger Thouin : une odyssée expérimentale qui brouille les époques
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "image", "url": "https://www.troiscouleurs.fr/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/734a15b589fcaea06b050dfa5c4e664c-1024x553.webp", "alt": "734a15b589fcaea06b050dfa5c4e664c", "caption": "", "credit": "Trois Couleurs"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Passionné d’images d’archives, Bérenger Thouin a choisi, pour son premier long métrage, d’entremêler des plans issus de documentaires d’époque (provenant du fonds Gaumont-Pathé Archives) à une fiction romanesque qu’il a écrite et tournée."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "On y découvre le destin de Jeanne Lavaur (Souheila Yacoub, magnétique), qui grandit dans une boucherie tenue par ses parents avant de faire irruption dans la haute société, à la faveur de sa rencontre avec un comte (Vassili Schneider). Une trajectoire fictive qui entraîne l’héroïne dans les tumultes du xx e siècle, de la crue de la Seine en 1910 aux deux guerres mondiales. Au fil de ses aventures sentimentales (dont sa grande passion pour Céleste, une révolutionnaire italienne), de ses joies et de ses épreuves de mère, Jeanne traverse toute une gamme d’émotions et affronte les tragédies de l’histoire, quitte à faire des choix moraux parfois discutables."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "Cette fresque foisonnante, menée tambour battant, devient alors le terrain d’une fascinante expérimentation formelle : en faisant dialoguer images d’hier et d’aujourd’hui, réalité et fiction, le cinéaste provoque un vertige temporel qui brouille les frontières entre les époques. Un pari de cinéma aussi singulier que vibrant, d’où surgit une profonde mélancolie, née de la collision entre les élans, les bonheurs et les regrets d’une vie."}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "L’Âge d’or de Bérenger Thouin, sortie le 11 novembre, Pyramide (1 h 53)"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "Retrouvez-nous sur"}]
article_text:
Passionné d’images d’archives, Bérenger Thouin a choisi, pour son premier long métrage, d’entremêler des plans issus de documentaires d’époque (provenant du fonds Gaumont-Pathé Archives) à une fiction romanesque qu’il a écrite et tournée.

On y découvre le destin de Jeanne Lavaur (Souheila Yacoub, magnétique), qui grandit dans une boucherie tenue par ses parents avant de faire irruption dans la haute société, à la faveur de sa rencontre avec un comte (Vassili Schneider). Une trajectoire fictive qui entraîne l’héroïne dans les tumultes du xx e siècle, de la crue de la Seine en 1910 aux deux guerres mondiales. Au fil de ses aventures sentimentales (dont sa grande passion pour Céleste, une révolutionnaire italienne), de ses joies et de ses épreuves de mère, Jeanne traverse toute une gamme d’émotions et affronte les tragédies de l’histoire, quitte à faire des choix moraux parfois discutables.

Cette fresque foisonnante, menée tambour battant, devient alors le terrain d’une fascinante expérimentation formelle : en faisant dialoguer images d’hier et d’aujourd’hui, réalité et fiction, le cinéaste provoque un vertige temporel qui brouille les frontières entre les époques. Un pari de cinéma aussi singulier que vibrant, d’où surgit une profonde mélancolie, née de la collision entre les élans, les bonheurs et les regrets d’une vie.

L’Âge d’or de Bérenger Thouin, sortie le 11 novembre, Pyramide (1 h 53)

article_text:
David Fincher directed The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , the Once Upon a Time in Hollywood follow-up written by Quentin Tarantino and starring Brad Pitt .

With Tarantino penning the script, Fincher had to make some sacrifices and cut 60 pages.

“The first draft I read was 230 pages. It was essentially two movies,” Fincher told Empire in a joint interview with Tarantino. “Somewhere in there was the Venn diagram of what Brad wanted to do, what I want to do, what Quentin wanted to do. Not ‘want to do,’ but the areas we would focus on.”

Related Stories

‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’ Trailer: Brad Pitt Revisits The Character That Won Him An Oscar In David Fincher’s Latest

Brad Pitt’s Tarantino Character Follow-Up Film Gets Title: ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’

With the cuts, The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth , which follows Pitt reprising his role as stuntman Cliff Booth, ended up having a runtime of around 2 hours and 20 minutes.

Watch on Deadline

The film, which is slated to premiere in Imax on November 25, followed by the Netflix release on December 23, also stars Elizabeth Debicki, Scott Caan, Carla Gugino, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Peter Weller.

Tarantino explained that he doesn’t think of TFMAOCB as a “hangout movie at all,” adding, “ Once Upon A Time In Hollywood was a hangout movie, but you know you’re going to Cielo Drive (site of the Manson murders). It has this force, thus I didn’t need a lot of plot. This script was very different.”

Once Upon a Time in Hollywood premiered in 2019 and was written and directed by Tarantino. The film featured a cast that included Pitt, Leonardo DiCaprio, Margot Robbie, Austin Butler, Dakota Fanning, Timothy Olyphant, Mike Moh, Margaret Qualley, Al Pacino, Emile Hirsch, Bruce Dern and Luke Perry.

article_text:
The chair of the El Paso County Republican Party has said he intends to sue Sacha Baron Cohen over footage of the local politician used in new satirical comedy Ali G: Who Iz I?

In the film, Michael Aboud is shown taking part in a training programme with another Cohen character, ex-Mossad terrorist expert Col Erran Morad, who instructs Aboud and fellow Maga sympathisers in self-defence techniques including the wearing, over clothes, of protective plastic buttocks. He also schools them in how to fire bullets from the middle of these buttocks by the repeated up and down manipulation of a rubber penis.

Aboud and a fellow student, former preacher and aspirant actor Joshua Loudermilk, are then recruited by Morad to help in a mission to prevent the birth in the US of the baby of a (fictional) South American drugs kingpin.

This involves Aboud and Loudermilk abducting his heavily-pregnant girlfriend and driving her in a phoney ambulance to a remote unstaffed medical facility, where she gives birth (to a lifelike prosthetic).

They then abandon her, Morad having placed her live baby in a zipped bag, and drive with it towards Mexico. Loudermilk is later seen attempting to discharge fire from his fake buttocks, while Aboud takes the decision to drop the baby – at that point being dangled from a drone at a substantial height – to the ground to prevent it touching US soil. The actions could not be anything other than extremely serious for a real infant.

Until the Guardian contacted Aboud on Tuesday, the businessman was unaware of his participation in anything other than what he believed to be a nonfiction film. In a statement, Aboud called Baron Cohen “and his entire film crew … a bunch of liars [who] deceive people to benefit themselves. They claimed that this would be a documentary about the illegals crossing the border. Then they said they were adding in this self-defence guy from Israel.”

He added: “It is my opinion that Sasha Cohen [sic] is a pervert. Plus he talked about how Muslims are all gay because they follow the sex practices of Mohamid [sic]. No one should spend one penny watching anything he produces or appears in. I plan to sue him.”

Pressed further on whether he stands by his actions in the film, Aboud declined to comment.

The film repeatedly stresses that neither Aboud nor Loudermilk are “in on it”. Loudermilk has not responded to requests for comment, but his social media feed suggests a level of understanding about the project not shared by most of his fellow participants.

Earlier this week, Loudermilk posted on Facebook that “I got to spend 12 hours one on one with Sasha [sic] and he taught me soooo much about the fun of making others laugh” as well as a link to a video promo for the film, saying, “I am in the trailer.” On 10 January, he also posted a headshot of himself, saying: “Howdy. Done with Sasha Cohen movie and ready for more.”

Representatives for the film have told the Guardian that Loudermilk was unaware of the true nature of the film.

Aboud’s shock at his involvement is particularly surprising given that he, along with Loudermilk, features in the second trailer for the film, which was released a fortnight ago.

That clip alone contains considerable clues to those involved that all is not what it seems. In his address to the recruits, Morad, who was a fixture of Baron Cohen’s 2018 show Who is America?, advises the group that they should not be fooled, for the immigrants they are set against “are not coming here to mow your lawn, trim your trees, rake your leaves, clean your house, care for your babies, bus your tables, wash your cars, paint your houses, build your fences, install your roofs, drywall, plumbing or electric. They are coming to kill you.”

Another section of the film involves Ali G hosting a “free speech” web show in which he is given a questionable script to read by South African producer Dirk Visser, who could not be contacted for comment.

The character also presides over a gameshow of Visser’s invention in which contestants, against the clock, must stuff mannequins depicting “undesirables” including rappers, gay people, Muslims and Mexican babies into pretend shower cubicles, before pressing a button to seemingly activate the release of the poisonous gas Zyklon B. The segment ends with a mass Nazi salute.

One of those who takes part is the disgraced former Republican congressman George Santos, who tells the camera his takeaway from playing the game is that next time he would try to grab more babies, as they’re easier to fit in the shower. In correspondence with the Guardian, Santos also suggested he was unaware of the true nature of the film, “as me and my team had no involvement”, and declined to justify his behaviour.

article_text:
G iven the 2020s horror boom, Indonesia’s prolific Joko Anwar – who has worked more often in that genre than any other – should be better known. Using horror for social commentary, as Anwar has done often in the past, this prison-slasher-satire features the kind of scabrous broadsides against injustice you see in Bong Joon-ho’s films, and Park Chan-wook’s recent No Other Choice . But in skewering the corruption and hypocrisy of the director’s native country, it has its own likable silliness and raucous energy. As the inmates keep saying: this is Indonesia, not Norway!

Fitted up for the murder of his boss, who is found gutted and spreadeagled on a ceiling fan, timid investigative journalist Dimas (Endy Arfian) winds up in the slammer. But murder, immediately followed by the flamboyant flaying of the victim, dogs him wherever he goes: the prison hitman assigned to dispose of him is in turn found in the washroom rendered into flesh origami. Charismatic prison refusenik Anggoro (Abimana Aryasatya) takes Dimas under his wing; as the victims stack up, an apparently clairvoyant member of his clique called Six (Yoga Pratama) admits that all of them manifested a red aura, signifying anger, prior to dying.

You suspect Anwar himself is no stranger to the old red aura from time to time: from the warden-facilitated drug-dealing network to the separate wing of pampered elitist offenders, his film overspills with droll outrage over Indonesian corruption. Dimas’s exposé of an illegal forestry scheme is what appears to have dislodged the demonic entity that is now attached to him, and feeding off the local abundance of negative energy. But Six figures out that partaking in wholesome activities, like praying and dancing, lowers their chances of being picked off.

Little more than a string of showpiece slaughters, Ghost in the Cell’s thin plot is really an excuse for Anwar to reel off his hitlist: he takes aim at cronyism, institutional brutality, private militias, secret mistresses, lapsed political idealism and the general degrading influence of money. But his film kidney-punches even harder when fully disguised and dramatised as comedy. This includes scenes where the aura-obsessed lags take a sudden interest in Qur’anic and twerking classes, and the most unhinged punch-up since John Carpenter’s They Live, during which Anggoro must periodically break into dancing to de-escalate his rage. Dynamically shot by Anwar, this is a very enjoyable blend of grand-guignol camp and political manifesto.

article_text:
Odysseus spent 10 years getting home. Universal is giving “ The Odyssey ” about 10 weeks to get its name on a ballot.

The studio’s official Oscar campaign for Christopher Nolan’s epic kicks off in earnest the week of Nov. 9, Variety has learned, with a run of screenings and Q & As that puts Nolan, producer Emma Thomas and star Matt Damon in front of voters nearly every night for two weeks.

WWE Enters Microdrama Space With 'Agent of Shadows,' Drew McIntyre Takes Central Role

Robert Downey Jr ., who won supporting actor for “Oppenheimer” (2024), will moderate the Los Angeles kickoff on Nov. 11 at the TCL Chinese Theatre, with an Imax 70mm screening. Oscar-winner Guillermo del Toro will be on hand at the AMC Universal CityWalk session on Nov. 12. Steven Spielberg will handle Nolan at the DGA Theater on Nov. 17, in 70mm.

That’s seven Oscar statuettes sitting in the moderator’s chair, and the campaign strategy is plain enough to see.

“The Odyssey” opened in July to a $264.1 million global debut, the biggest of Nolan’s career. It has since crossed $1.1 billion, becoming his highest-grossing film. Universal and Nolan’s team are continuing to focus on the format. Nearly every Los Angeles date is tagged Imax 70mm, 70mm or 35mm, reminding the membership that Homer’s poem was shot entirely using Imax film cameras and built to be judged on a screen the size of a building and not on a laptop or their home TV using the Academy digital portal.

The fall campaign leans on format and prestige in an effort to convince voters it’s more than a box office hit. Only two films that cleared $1 billion have won best picture, “Titanic” and “The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King.” Others, like “Avatar,” “Top Gun: Maverick” and “Barbie” all got in but went home without the top prize. It’s a reminder that some voters might treat a summer tentpole as only that. However, Nolan has one major credential that could clear all of those hurdles. “Oppenheimer,” also a summer blockbuster, took home seven Oscars back at the 2025 ceremony, including best picture and director.

One of the campaign’s centerpieces during this awards blitz isn’t a screening of the film at all.

On Nov. 10, Universal’s Spielberg Theater will host the world premiere of “Behind the Scenes of The Odyssey,” a 75-minute making-of documentary introduced by Nolan himself. The film’s star Damon, who plays Odysseus, will moderate the Q&A afterward, which will include all the key artisan players: producer Emma Thomas, casting director John Papsidera, editor Jennifer Lame, production designer Ruth De Jong, costume designer Ellen Mirojnick, hair department head Gloria Casny, makeup department head Luisa Abel, sound mixer Willie Burton, supervising sound editor Craig Henighan, composer and songwriter Ludwig Göransson and visual effects supervisor Andrew Jackson. A reception will follow.

If the movie ends up with a dozen nominations, and Variety thinks it will , many of them will come from the people invited to that room.

article_text:
Michael Douglas is giving fans an update on Jack Nicholson .

While promoting his new memoir, “One Helluva Ride,” at a recent event, Douglas was asked about Nicholson and his relationship with the “Something’s Gotta Give” actor.

“I would have liked to have acted with Jack,” Douglas said. “He’s not working anymore. He’s well. He has disappeared. I know that.” He continued: “I still see him, but he is fine. He is up there by his house and walking around in his slippers. It happens. He deserves it. I understand. He is a few years older than me, but I understand.” (Douglas is 82, while Nicholson is 89.)

Related Stories

Ben Frow Stepping Down as Chief Content Officer of 5, Skydance's U.K. Network, After 14 Years

While the two never shared the screen, Douglas produced the 1975 film “One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest,” in which Nicholson starred as Randle McMurphy. The film earned nine Oscar nominations and won five, including best actor for Nicholson and best picture.

Though Nicholson’s never made a formal statement announcing his retirement, the Oscar-winner hasn’t appeared in a film since “How Do You Know” in 2010. He’s also infrequently photographed, though his daughter, Lorraine, shared a snap of the star for his birthday in April.

The photo, posted on her Instagram story, shows Nicholson clapping and smiling while sitting next to Joni Mitchell . Lorraine didn’t indicate when the photo was taken, but simply wrote on the photo, “¡¡ 89 !!” after posting a photo of a younger Jack in a Coca-Cola shirt with, “89?”

Nicholson’s last public appearance was during the “Saturday Night Live” 50 th anniversary television special on NBC in February 2025, which he attended with his daughter.

editorial_title_zh: 古巴艺术市场……一部未完成的历史，作者佩德罗·埃德加·里索·佩尼亚
editorial_excerpt_zh: 本书首次重建了一个既迷人又极不稳定的体系之演变过程：在一个买卖、合法化、出口和收藏从未是中立行为的国家，艺术市场是如何运作的。通过从共和时期的画廊……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "heading", "text": "当一件古巴艺术品的价格不仅取决于签名，还取决于历史、政治、短缺、外汇、来源以及外国买家的目光时，它的价值究竟几何？市场到底从哪里开始？是在艺术家的工作室、哈瓦那的一家画廊、一个国际博览会上，还是当一场拍卖会将一件作品变成公开的数据时？", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "《古巴艺术市场……一部未完成的历史》首次将一个既迷人又极不稳定的体系之演变汇聚于单个文集之中：在一个买卖、合法化、出口和收藏从未是中立行为的国家，艺术市场是如何运作的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "通过回顾从1959年之前的共和时期画廊到近年来的数字平台和在线拍卖，佩德罗·埃德加·里索·佩尼亚（Pedro Edgar Rizo Peña）揭示了一个历经机构、经济危机、许可证、博览会、收藏家、中间商、工坊、档案和灰色地带的历史背后的隐秘层面。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "本书聚焦于几个决定性时刻：革命转向、国家集中化、“特殊时期”（Período Especial）、外国收藏热潮的爆发、哈瓦那拍卖行（Subasta Habana）的经验、画廊的不完全专业化，以及诸如威夫雷多·兰（Wifredo Lam）等艺术家的国际拍卖纪录。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "是什么解释了古巴艺术在岛外创下百万美元的高价，而其内部市场却依然在脆弱、即兴和对外依赖中运转？作者在这里仅为我们提供了这本理解古巴艺术市场的必备出版物的一瞥。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Mercado-de-arte-en-cuba-1.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "一部未完成的历史究竟价值几何？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "佩德罗·埃德加·里索·佩尼亚（Pedro Edgar Rizo Peña）", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "几十年来，人们向我们兜售这样一种神话：古巴艺术游离于市场之外，身处一个水晶球罩之中，作品从工坊走向博物馆，从外国收藏走向拍卖大厅，从未沾染过谈判、许可证、中间商、等级制度或经济计算。这纯属谎言。资金最终还是会到账，只是披上了羞怯的外衣，变成了一个官方叙事宁愿不愿正视的数字。多年来，我也不愿正视它。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《古巴艺术市场……一部未完成的历史》恰恰立足于这一点，切入那个我们都在假装看不见的盲区。它并不追问一件古巴作品价值几何。它带着一种难能可贵的无礼，追问究竟是谁拥有确定这种价值的权力，在什么条件下，又是从哪种阐述立场出发。哈瓦那的一家国有画廊。一位官员。一位古巴裔美国收藏家。一个国际博览会。纽约的一家拍卖行。每个人看着同一件作品，却决定着不同的价格，因为每个人都在未曾言明的情况下捍卫着自身的合法化体系。正是在这种目光的摩擦中，这本书诞生了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“未完成的历史”这一表述并非学术上的谨小慎微。而是一份宣战书，尽管它的表达带有某种仍在体制内部工作之人的审慎。“未完成”并不局限于叙事本身——叙事受到分散的档案、私人操作以及我们所有人皆知却鲜少提及的体制沉默的拉扯。它也延伸至古巴市场本身，这个由艺术家、买家、画廊、博览会、中间商和拍卖行组成的装置，从未真正完全组装完毕。更坦率地说，应该讲：他们从未让我们完全组装完毕。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这段历程始于1959年之前，当时的共和时期画廊和沙龙作为流通平台；新兴的私人收藏当时已经在自行运作。革命爆发了，从根本上改变了一切，且未加征询。国家占据了艺术推广、合法化和商业化的中心，而私有财产和商业关系则被迫接受深刻的重组——如今回读，我不得不称之为外科手术般的重组。或者按某些时候的视角来看，是惩罚性的重组。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "由此诞生了贯穿全书乃至我们作为古巴人自身生平的矛盾之一。市场可以在官方话语中遭到驳斥，但作品仍在继续出售。发生变化的是谁在居中斡旋，以及用什么样的行政语言来命名这项操作。交流并未消失。它被隐藏在一个体制机构内部，该机构负责筛选艺术家、批准出口、组织展览并管理他人创作所产生的大部分收入。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Mercado-de-arte-en-cuba-2.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "签署这本书的人从内部了解这个系统，我希望大家能在字里行间注意到这一点。我曾担任古巴文化资产基金会（Fondo Cubano de Bienes Culturales）的画廊商业总监和外贸负责人。我不是从一个从未签署过文件的评论员那种舒适的距离来进行写作的。再加上我的背景跨越了法律、经济和史学——拥有马德里内夫里哈大学（Universidad de Nebrija）艺术市场与相关企业管理硕士学位，目前正在胡安卡洛斯国王大学（Universidad Rey Juan Carlos）和古巴艺术大学（Universidad de las Artes de Cuba）攻读经济与企业博士学位——这迫使我必须超越形式上的作品本身去进行观察。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "合同、授权、货币、税收、文化政策、管理模式。所有这些都是艺术生命的一部分，谁若否认这一点，就是在撒谎，或者从未在这个系统内部工作过。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "特殊时期是这段历史的分水岭，正如它对许多其他事情一样。经济危机、失控的旅游业、对获取外汇的残酷需求，彻底改变了创作与商业之间的关系。工作室、画廊、工坊乃至整个机构开始迎来外国买家，他们寻找作品，并且几乎总是同时寻求一种接触文化现场的体验——这种文化现场被当作非同寻常之物兜售给他们。必须补充的是：既非同寻常，又很便宜。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种国际收藏带来了机遇。它也加剧了我们直到今天仍难以承认的依赖性。外国买家获得了引导价格和整条艺术生涯的巨大能力。国内收藏的匮乏将外部需求变成了生存的源泉，同时也是一种权威的形式。这种品味总是伴随着外汇而来。它总是伴随着某种东西。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "诸如彼得·路德维格（Peter Ludwig）对古巴艺术的收购、基因艺术画廊（Génesis Galerías de Arte）的兴起或哈瓦那拍卖行（Subasta Habana）的创立等事件，展示了构建商业化与可视性专业工具的尝试。拍卖使某些价格公开，并留下了可查阅的销售记录。然而，这种透明度是局部的，正如岛上几乎所有事情一样。在拍卖厅之外，私人销售、非正式协议以及那些如今几乎无法追溯来源的作品仍在流通。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这种暗箱操作区是该书提出的最诚实的问题之一。市场需要信息来产生信任。此前的价格、真实性、来源、合同、所有权记录。当这些数据变得支离破碎时，价值便过分依赖于人际关系、未经核实的说法或拥有特权渠道的中介。而信息的缺失从来不会平均分摊其影响。它青睐那些从内部了解系统的人，却将经验较少的艺术家、继承人和买家置于暴露的境地。那些总是为派对买单的人。", "translated": true}, "paragraph", "text": "一旦作品漂洋过海，历史的规模就会发生变化。那里的对比是残酷的。当国内市场的运作始终伴随着脆弱性时，古巴艺术家却在纽约、伦敦、帕里斯取得了显著的数字。维fredo·兰（Wifredo Lam）是最明显的例子，但并非唯一。他的国际纪录证明，古巴艺术的价值可以在远离作品诞生地的领土之外构建。远在异国，有时甚至与之对抗。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "地理上的位移也改变了叙事。在迈阿密、马德里、纽约以及许许多多的城市，流散群体建立起了画廊、档案库、收藏，以及有能力赋予那些在古巴国内流传受限或直接被否认的艺术家以合法性的网络。古巴市场不再与国家边界重合。它变成了一个分散的星群，交织着流亡、移民、政治冲突，以及关于谁才有权代表国家文化的陈年争端。就好像真有人能完全拥有这种权力一样。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "数字平台、在线销售、NFT进一步扩大了这个分散的领土。互联网承诺减少对传统中介的依赖。但它也带来了其他过滤器。算法、私有平台、支付系统、真实性问题、新的集中化形式。渠道变了。不对称性没有变。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "它们从来没有完全改变过。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《古巴艺术市场……一部未完成的历史》的主要贡献之一，在于将以往史学通常分开处理、仿佛彼此毫无关系的进程汇聚到了一起。文化政策、收藏、画廊、拍卖、国际流通在这里被纳入同一个权力结构中进行阐述。价格不再是艺术家生平底部的轶事数据。它充当了文献。它诉说着权力、稀缺、认可与获取。它首先诉说着，谁来做决定。", true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "读完这本书后，很难再坚持认为市场是古巴艺术之外的东西。即使在无法清晰命名的时候，它也一直存在。在一个国营画廊里，在一个酒店房间里，在一个旅行者的行李箱里，在拍卖会上，在从另一个国家发起的转账中。这段历史并未缺席。它一直是分散的，就像所有从外部审视的古巴事物一样。就像我们几乎所有人一样。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://artishockrevista.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Mercado-de-arte-en-cuba-5.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "Artishock", "translated": true}]

article_text:
¿Cuánto vale una obra de arte cubano cuando su precio no depende solo de la firma, sino también de la historia, la política, la escasez, la divisa, la procedencia y la mirada del comprador extranjero? ¿Dónde empieza realmente el mercado? ¿En el estudio del artista, en una galería de La Habana, en una feria internacional o cuando una subasta convierte una obra en cifra pública?

Mercado de arte en Cuba… una historia incompleta reconstruye, por primera vez en un solo corpus, la evolución de un sistema tan fascinante como inestable: el mercado del arte en un país donde vender, legitimar, exportar y coleccionar nunca han sido actos neutrales.

A través de un recorrido que va desde las galerías republicanas anteriores a 1959 hasta las plataformas digitales y las subastas en línea de los últimos años, Pedro Edgar Rizo Peña revela las capas ocultas de una historia atravesada por instituciones, crisis económicas, permisos, ferias, coleccionistas, intermediarios, talleres, archivos y zonas grises.

El libro se detiene en momentos decisivos: el giro revolucionario, la centralización estatal, el Período Especial, la irrupción del coleccionismo extranjero, la experiencia de Subasta Habana, la profesionalización incompleta de las galerías y los récords internacionales de artistas como Wifredo Lam.

¿Qué explica que el arte cubano haya alcanzado precios millonarios fuera de la isla mientras su mercado interno seguía funcionando con fragilidad, improvisación y dependencia exterior? El autor nos ofrece aquí apenas una pincelada de lo que contiene esta publicación indispensable para entender el mercado de arte cubano.

¿CUÁNTO VALE UNA HISTORIA INCOMPLETA?

Pedro Edgar Rizo Peña

Durante décadas nos vendieron la fábula de un arte cubano que flotaba fuera del mercado, en una campana de cristal donde las obras iban del taller al museo, de la colección extranjera a la sala de subastas, sin ensuciarse nunca con negociaciones, permisos, intermediarios, jerarquías, cálculos económicos. Mentira. El dinero llegaba igual, al final, camuflado de pudor, convertido en una cifra que el relato oficial prefería no mirar de frente. Yo tampoco quise mirarla durante años.

Mercado de arte en Cuba… una historia incompleta se planta justo ahí, en esa zona ciegaque todos fingíamos no ver. No pregunta cuánto vale una obra cubana. Pregunta, con una insolencia que se agradece, quién ha tenido el poder de fijar ese valor, bajo qué condiciones, desde qué lugar de enunciación. Una galería estatal en La Habana. Un funcionario. Un coleccionista cubanoamericano. Una feria internacional. Una casa de subastas en Nueva York. Cada uno mira la misma pieza y decide un precio distinto, porque cada uno defiende, sin decirlo, su propio sistema de legitimación. De esa fricción de miradas nace el libro.

La expresión «historia incompleta» no es cautela académica. Es una declaración de guerra, aunque la enuncie con la mesura de quien todavía trabaja dentro de las instituciones. Lo incompleto no se limita al relato -tensionado por archivos dispersos, operaciones privadas, silencios institucionales que todos conocemos y pocos nombran-. Alcanza al propio mercado cubano, ese dispositivo con artistas, compradores, galerías, ferias, intermediarios y subastas que nunca terminó de armarse del todo. Que nunca nos dejaron armar del todo, habría que decir con más honestidad.

El recorrido arranca antes de 1959, con las galerías republicanas y los salones como plataformas de circulación; el coleccionismo privado, incipiente, ya se movía por su cuenta. Llegó la Revolución y cambió todo, de raíz, sin preguntar. El Estado ocupó el centro de la promoción, la legitimación y la comercialización del arte, mientras la propiedad privada y las relaciones mercantiles quedaban sometidas a una reorganización profunda que, leída hoy, no puedo dejar de llamar quirúrgica. O punitiva, según el día en que uno la mire.

De ahí nace una de las contradicciones que atraviesa el libro entero, y también nuestra propia biografía como cubanos. El mercado podía impugnarse en el discurso oficial, pero las obras seguían vendiéndose. Cambió quién mediaba, con qué lenguaje administrativo se nombraba la operación. El intercambio no desapareció. Se escondió dentro de un aparato institucional que seleccionaba artistas, autorizaba exportaciones, organizaba exposiciones y administraba buena parte de los ingresos que generaba la creación de otros.

Quien firma este libro conoce ese sistema desde dentro, y espero se note en cada página. Fui director comercial de galerías y responsable de comercio exterior en el Fondo Cubano de Bienes Culturales . No escribo desde la distancia cómoda del comentarista que nunca firmó un papel. A esa experiencia súmese una formación que cruza el derecho, la economía y la historiografía -Máster en Mercado de Arte y Gestión de Empresas Relacionadas por la Universidad de Nebrija, en Madrid, y en la actualidad doctorando en Economía y Empresa por la Universidad Rey Juan Carlos y la Universidad de las Artes de Cuba- que me obliga a mirar más allá de la obra formal.

Contratos, autorizaciones, monedas, impuestos, políticas culturales, modelos de gestión. Todo eso es vida artística, y quien lo niegue miente, o no ha trabajado nunca dentro del sistema.

El Período Especial es la bisagra de esta historia, como lo fue de tantas otras. La crisis económica, el turismo desbocado, la necesidad brutal de captar divisas transformaron la relación entre creación y comercio. Estudios, galerías, talleres, instituciones enteras empezaron a recibir compradores extranjeros que buscaban obras y, casi siempre, también la experiencia de rozar una escena cultural que se les vendía como excepcional. Excepcional y barata, habría que añadir.

Ese coleccionismo internacional trajo oportunidades. También acentuó dependencias que todavía hoy nos cuesta admitir. El comprador extranjero ganó una capacidad enorme para orientar precios y carreras enteras. La escasez de coleccionismo nacional convirtió la demanda exterior en fuente de supervivencia y, al mismo tiempo, en forma de autoridad. El gusto llegaba acompañado de divisas. Siempre llega acompañado de algo.

Episodios como la adquisición de arte cubano por Peter Ludwig , el surgimiento de Génesis Galerías de Arte o la creación de Subasta Habana muestran los intentos de construir instrumentos profesionales de comercialización y visibilidad. Las subastas volvieron públicos ciertos precios y dejaron antecedentes de venta consultables. Esa transparencia, sin embargo, fue parcial, como casi todo en la Isla. Fuera de la sala siguieron las ventas privadas, los acuerdos informales, la circulación de obras cuya procedencia resulta hoy casi imposible de reconstruir.

Esa zona de opacidad es uno de los problemas más honestos que plantea el libro. Un mercado necesita información para generar confianza. Precios anteriores, autenticidad, procedencia, contratos, registros de propiedad. Cuando esos datos quedan fragmentados, el valor depende demasiado de relaciones personales, versiones no verificadas o intermediarios con acceso privilegiado. Y la falta de información nunca reparte sus efectos por igual. Favorece a quien conoce el sistema desde dentro, y deja expuestos a artistas, herederos y compradores con menos experiencia. A los que siempre pagan la fiesta.

La historia cambia de escala en cuanto las obras cruzan el mar. El contraste, ahí, es brutal. Mientras el mercado interno funcionó siempre con fragilidad, artistas cubanos alcanzan cifras notables en Nueva York, Londres, París. Wifredo Lam es el caso más visible, no el único. Sus récords internacionales prueban que el valor del arte cubano puede construirse lejos del territorio donde las obras nacieron. Lejos, y a veces contra él.

El desplazamiento geográfico también transforma el relato. En Miami, Madrid, Nueva York y en tantas otras ciudades, la diáspora levantó galerías, archivos, colecciones, redes capaces de legitimar a artistas que dentro de Cuba tuvieron una circulación limitada, o directamente negada. El mercado cubano deja de coincidir con las fronteras nacionales. Se vuelve una constelación dispersa, cruzada por exilios, migraciones, conflictos políticos, disputas de siempre sobre quién tiene autoridad para representar la cultura del país. Como si alguien la tuviera del todo.

Las plataformas digitales, las ventas en línea, los NFT amplían todavía más ese territorio disperso. Internet promete reducir la dependencia de los intermediarios tradicionales. Pero trae consigo otros filtros. Algoritmos, plataformas privadas, sistemas de pago, problemas de autenticidad, nuevas formas de concentración. Cambian los canales. Las asimetrías, no.

Nunca cambian del todo.

Uno de los aportes principales de Mercado de arte en Cuba… una historia incompleta consiste en reunir procesos que la historiografía solía tratar por separado, como si no tuvieran nada que ver entre sí. La política cultural, el coleccionismo, las galerías, las subastas, la circulación internacional aparecen aquí articulados dentro de una misma estructura de poder. El precio deja de ser el dato anecdótico al pie de la biografía de un artista. Funciona como documento. Habla de poder, de escasez, de reconocimiento, de acceso. Habla, sobre todo, de quién decide.

La amplitud del recorrido obliga a condensar episodios que, por sí solos, podrían sostener libros enteros. Es una limitación, sí. Pero coincide con la naturaleza abierta del proyecto. El libro no cierra una cronología ni finge resolver todas las zonas oscuras. Organiza un campo de estudio y deja las preguntas ahí, expuestas, esperando documentos, testimonios, análisis más finos que alguien, algún día, tendrá que escribir.

Ahí está, creo, el sentido más productivo del subtítulo. Lo incompleto funciona como posición crítica frente a una historia escrita con archivos insuficientes, operaciones invisibles y relatos institucionales que rara vez reconocen la dimensión económica del arte, no como disculpa por lo que falta. Completarla exigirá mirar las obras junto con las facturas, las exposiciones junto con los contratos. También los discursos curatoriales, cruzados con las rutas que siguió el dinero. Todo el dinero que nadie quiso contar.

Después de este libro cuesta sostener que el mercado sea algo exterior al arte cubano. Estuvo presente incluso cuando no se podía nombrar con claridad. En una galería estatal, en la habitación de un hotel, en la maleta de un viajero, en una subasta, en una transferencia hecha desde otro país. Esa historia no estuvo ausente. Estuvo dispersa, como casi todo lo cubano que se mira desde fuera. Como casi todos nosotros.
excerpt_original: Este libro reconstruye por primera vez la evolución de un sistema tan fascinante como inestable: el mercado del arte en un país donde vender, legitimar, exportar y coleccionar nunca han sido actos neutrales. A través de un recorrido que va desde las galerías republicanas…

走水水源地2026 2026年10月31日（土）–11月3日（火・祝） 旧走水小学校（神奈川県横須賀市走水2-2-2） https://bankart1929.com/ 開館時間：10:00–16:30 会期中無休 観覧料：無料（イベントは一部有料） 主催：BankART1929 展覧会URL： https://bankart1929.com/project/hashirimizu-water-sourse-2026/ 出品作家：大巻伸嗣、片岡純也＋岩竹理恵、チャチャ、保良雄、水戸部春菜、ルカ・レグリーズ、原口典之

BankART1929は、横須賀市走水地区の旧走水小学校を舞台に、水と土地をめぐる4日間のアートプロジェクト「走水水源地2026」を開催する。 2004年から20年間、横浜を拠点に歴史的建造物や遊休空間を活用しながら、アートを通して都市と人、人と場の新たな関係を探ってきたBankART1929は、現在、特定の拠点にとどまらず、さまざまな土地や空間と関わりながら活動を展開している。今年2月には、横浜市の稼働中の下水処理施設である港北水再生センターで保良雄の個展「 TOTEM ORGA(H)／トーテムオルガ 」を開催し、都市の見えない循環と暮らしについての考察を深めた。 今回舞台となる 走水 は、豊かな湧水に恵まれ、都市化が進んだ東京湾岸にあって、海と山とがつながる三浦半島本来の地形の記憶を残す土地であり、古事記や日本書紀にもその地名が刻まれている。会場となる旧走水小学校は、1873年に開校し「海に一番近い小学校」として親しまれてきたが、2025年3月に横須賀市立馬堀小学校に統合され、151年の歴史に幕を下ろした。タイトルの由来となった、この地に実在する「走水水源地」の「水源」を、BankART1929は、目には見えない循環や蓄積が重なり、新たな流れとして姿を現す場所として捉える。本展は、地域を中心としたイベント「Through the Water 2026 Autumn」（主催：Through the Water 実行委員会）と連動し、展示、ワークショップ、トークを通して、走水という土地に流れてきた文化の水脈をたどるとともに、人々が土地と出会い、対話し、未来を思い描く場をひらく試みとなる。

大巻伸嗣 （1971年岐阜県生まれ）は、「存在」とは何かをテーマに制作活動を展開している。環境や他者といった外界と、記憶や意識などの内界、その境界である身体の関係性を探り、三者のあいだで揺れ動く、曖昧で捉えどころのない「存在」に迫るための身体的時空間の創出を試みる。近年の主な展覧会に、「SPRING わきあがる鼓動」（ポーラ美術館、神奈川、2025–2026）、個展「Open the Box 2025: Bloom of Light」（大館美術館、香港、2025）、個展「大巻伸嗣 Interface of Being 真空のゆらぎ」（国立新美術館、東京、2023）などがある。 片岡純也＋岩竹理恵 は、ともに2010年に筑波大学大学院芸術専攻を修了し、2013年のパリでの滞在制作を機にユニットとしての発表を開始した。身の回りのささやかな出来事から着想し、シンプルな現象へと置き換えるキネティック作品と平面作品を組み合わせ、事物や図像のあいだに潜む関係をたどりながら、個々の作品の題材がゆるやかに響きあう場をつくる。近年の主な展覧会に、個展「カエルの痙攣、レモンの光ー位相する運動」（カスヤの森現代美術館、神奈川、2026）、「Yokohama Re:Portside Project Vol.1」（横浜クリエーションスクエア、神奈川、2025–2026）、「岩竹理恵＋片岡純也×コレクション 重力と素材のための図鑑」（神奈川県立近代美術館 鎌倉別館、2025）などがある。 チャチャ （2000年中国・福建省生まれ）は、2023年より東京に在住し、東京藝術大学大学院美術研究科博士後期課程に在籍している。水滴、気泡、風に舞うビニール袋といった目的を持たない複雑な自然運動や物理現象を起点に、人間の「自覚なき能動性」や生きている状態そのものを探求するインスタレーションを制作する。近年の主な展覧会に、「SICF27」（スパイラル、東京、2026）、二人展「そっと揺れる現象に目をこらす」（ギャラリー準備中、東京、2025）などがある。 保良雄 （滋賀県生まれ）は、福島をはじめとする複数の地域で定点的なフィールドワークを行い、土地や物質への直接的な接触を重視する。生物、無生物、人間を横並びの存在として捉え、自然環境や都市空間のなかにある、見えるもの／見えないものを含めた多様な存在との関係性を探求している。現在は千葉県を拠点に活動。近年の主な展覧会に、個展「TOTEM ORGA(H)／トーテムオルガ」（港北水再生センター、神奈川、2026）、「第36回リュブリャナ・グラフィック・ビエンナーレ」（スロベニア、2025）、「エコロジー：循環をめぐるダイアローグ」（銀座メゾンエルメスフォーラム、東京、2024）などがある。

水戸部春菜 （1995年神奈川県生まれ）は、状態の記録や保存をテーマに、何らかの背景による痕跡が残った環境や、人間の行動の本質的なリアリティを求めたインスタレーションやドローイングを制作している。東北芸術工科大学デザイン工学部グラフィックデザイン学科を卒業し、現在は横須賀市を拠点に活動。近年の主な展覧会に、個展「蝶の名前」（nanamica MOUNTAIN、2026）、個展「1&1」（galleryN、2025）、「SENSE ISLAND/LAND 感覚の島と感覚の地」（神奈川県横須賀市、2024）、「往古来今／見えない泉をさまよいさがす」（横須賀美術館、神奈川、2024）などがある。 ルカ・レグリーズ （1992年フランス生まれ）は、写真イメージそのものの物質性と、それが立ち現れる条件について探究を続けている。とりわけアナログ写真のプロセスにおいて、現実世界とそのイメージのあいだを往還しながら、フィルムに光が刻み込むものと、写真がその被写体（参照対象）と結ぶ関係の双方を考察する。パリ国立高等美術学校を卒業。 原口典之 （1946-2020／神奈川県生まれ）は、横須賀市に生まれ、戦後から激動の1960年代から70年代という時代を背景に、原寸大の軍用機を作品化した立体をはじめ、鉄、廃油、ポリウレタンなどの工業素材を用いた作品を制作した。絵画や彫刻の既成概念を再考し、事物の表層ではなく構造に目を向けながら、素材と空間の関係を際立たせる表現を展開。代表作《オイル・プール》は1977年の「ドクメンタ6」（カッセル）に出品され、国際的な評価を確立した。主な個展に「原口典之ー社会と物質」（BankART Studio NYK、横浜、2009）などがある。 また、会期中の11月1日から3日にかけては、地域とアートをめぐるイベントプログラムを開催する。美術家の 山本愛子 が走水で採集した植物から染料を抽出し、さまざまな色彩を生みだす公開ラボ「色のみなもと」をはじめ、水戸部春菜、山本愛子と横須賀市自然・人文博物館学芸員の 山本薫 による走水の植生をめぐるフィールドワーク、走水でとれた海藻を用いたルカ・レグリーズによるサイアノタイプ（日光写真）のワークショップを実施。トークでは、横須賀で地域に根ざしたアートの実践を続ける「YOKOSUKA ART VALLEY HIRAKU」と「やとと」の活動報告や、海と人との関わりを起点に学びの可能性を探る対話、海を隔てた対岸の房総半島で土地の地形や自然環境を起点に展開される「干潟と芸術」（木更津）と「小さな地球」（鴨川）の活動紹介を行う。

title_original: The night: Mariachiara Di Giorgio in mostra allo ZebraStudio di Roma
editorial_title_zh: The night：玛丽亚基娅拉·迪·乔治（Mariachiara Di Giorgio）罗马 ZebraStudio 展览
editorial_excerpt_zh: 艺术家兼插画家玛丽亚基娅拉·迪·乔治（Mariachiara Di Giorgio）在意大利首展无字书《The night》的原画，该书完全通过图像和叙事序列构建。本文源自…
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "10月23日至25日每天19时起，罗马 ZebraStudio 将举办意大利首展，呈现玛丽亚基娅拉·迪·乔治（Mariachiara Di Giorgio）无字书《The night》的原画，该书通过两个孩子的视角展现对夜晚的探索。本书讲述了两个兄弟姐妹趁保姆不注意溜进黑暗、穿过寂静、偶遇狐狸和野兔、在星空下起舞，并将夜晚变成探索空间的故事。最终，正是夜晚将他们引领回了家，迎来了回归熟悉环境的时刻。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本次展览通过迪·乔治创作的原画，带领观众近距离观察该书成型的视觉过程。在一本没有文字辅助、靠叙事推进的无字书中，图像承担了划分时间、暗示动作以及构建人物与空间关系的全部任务。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "从插画到电影", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "玛丽亚基娅拉·迪·乔治曾在罗马欧洲设计学院（IED）和巴黎装饰艺术学院（École des Arts Décoratifs）学习。在投身儿童出版领域之前，她曾担任电影和广告的分镜师与概念设计师，这段经历促成了她对图像序列、节奏和叙事构建极其专注的创作实践。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "自2012年起，她将精力集中于儿童插画，并参加了博洛尼亚童书展和纽约插画师协会（Society of Illustrators）等展览。多年来，她的作品获得了众多奖项，其中包括2018年和2022年的法国女巫奖（Prix Sorcières）、2022年英国与约托·凯特·格林纳威奖（Yoto Kate Greenaway Medal）相关的影子选择奖（Shadowers’ Choice Award），以及同年被评为最佳插画师的安徒生奖——幻想图像奖（Premio Andersen – Le immagini della fantasia）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "她最知名的作品包括《La zuppa Lepron》、《Professione coccodrillo》和《A mezzanotte》，其中后两本正是以无字书的形式创作的。最近，《纽约时报书评》将《Make New Friends》列入了2025年十佳儿童读物榜单。", "translated": true}, {"type": "heading", "text": "交由图像托付的叙事", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过《The night》，迪·乔治再次回归无文字的叙事形式，将阐明恐惧、好奇与发现之间关系的重任托付给图像的相继呈现。夜晚起到了叙事装置的作用：一个最初未知的空间，通过两位主角的经历，逐渐转变为一个充满自由和奇迹的地方。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "因此，ZebraStudio 的这场展览为人们提供了一个契机，得以观察从原创手稿到图书出版构思的转变，以及更广泛地了解插画如何在没有文字的情况下构筑一个故事。", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Dal 23 al 25 ottobre, dalle ore 19, ZebraStudio di Roma presenta in anteprima italiana le tavole originali di The night , silent book di Mariachiara Di Giorgio dedicato alla scoperta della notte attraverso lo sguardo di due bambini. Il libro racconta l’avventura di due fratelli che, sfuggiti alla tata, si inoltrano nel buio e ne attraversano il silenzio, incontrando una volpe e una lepre, danzando sotto le stelle e trasformando la notte in uno spazio di esplorazione. Sarà proprio la notte, alla fine, a ricondurli verso casa, dove li attende il ritorno alla dimensione familiare.

La mostra permette di osservare da vicino il processo visivo che ha portato alla costruzione del libro, attraverso le tavole originali realizzate da Di Giorgio. In un silent book, dove la narrazione procede senza il supporto del testo scritto, l’immagine assume interamente il compito di scandire il tempo, suggerire il movimento e costruire il rapporto tra i personaggi e lo spazio.

Dall’illustrazione al cinema

Mariachiara Di Giorgio si è formata allo IED di Roma e all’École des Arts Décoratifs di Parigi. Prima di dedicarsi all’editoria per l’infanzia ha lavorato come storyboard artist e concept designer per il cinema e la pubblicità, esperienza che ha contribuito a definire una pratica particolarmente attenta alla sequenza, al ritmo e alla costruzione narrativa delle immagini.

Dal 2012 ha concentrato la propria attività sull’illustrazione per l’infanzia, partecipando anche a esposizioni alla Fiera del Libro di Bologna e alla Society of Illustrators di New York. Nel corso degli anni i suoi lavori hanno ricevuto numerosi riconoscimenti, tra cui il Prix Sorcières nel 2018 e nel 2022, lo Shadowers’ Choice Award legato alla Yoto Kate Greenaway Medal nel Regno Unito nel 2022 e il Premio Andersen – Le immagini della fantasia come migliore illustratrice nello stesso anno.

Tra i suoi titoli più conosciuti figurano La zuppa Lepron , Professione coccodrillo e A mezzanotte , due di questi ultimi costruiti proprio nella forma del silent book. Più recentemente, il Book Review del New York Times ha inserito Make New Friends tra i dieci migliori libri per bambini del 2025.

Una narrazione affidata alle immagini

Con The night , Di Giorgio torna a lavorare su una forma narrativa priva di testo, affidando alla successione delle immagini il compito di rendere leggibile la relazione tra paura, curiosità e scoperta. La notte funziona da dispositivo narrativo: uno spazio inizialmente sconosciuto che, attraverso l’esperienza dei due protagonisti, si trasforma progressivamente in un luogo di libertà e meraviglia.

La mostra di ZebraStudio offre così l’occasione per osservare il passaggio dal disegno originale alla costruzione editoriale del libro e, più in generale, il modo in cui l’illustrazione può costruire una storia anche in assenza della parola scritta.

article_text:
Market

“Turning the Frown Upside-Down”: Art Taipei 2026

JEFFREY IAN ROSEN at Art Taipei 2026. Courtesy Art Taipei.

At the center of a spacious booth at Art Taipei 2026, a black banner declared in white capitals: “THE ARTIST HAS TO LIVE LIKE EVERYBODY ELSE.” The work, by the late New Zealand-born artist Billy Apple (1935–2021), was presented by Tokyo-based non-profit Goya Curtain in “Curated Japan,” a special section that brought together 12 Japanese galleries and initiatives alongside Taipei’s artist-run ss space space. Curated by Jeffrey Ian Rosen of Tokyo-based MISAKO & ROSEN, the presentation ranged from the canonical to the contemporary: a painting by Nakanishi Natsuyuki (1935–2016); a large monochrome mural by 94-year-old Shinohara Ushio, known for action paintings punched with paint-soaked boxing gloves; and deadpan interventions by London-based artist Alexei Izmaylov, surreptitiously fitted to sockets at booth corners. Near the aisle, COBRA’s The Game of Life 50 invited fairgoers to toss dice onto a numbered floor mat, each square marking a threshold in an artist’s career.

The section’s title, “Turning the Frown Upside-Down,” traced the rise of artist-initiated hybrid spaces in Japan after the 2008 financial crisis, a counter-strategy against a market increasingly dominated by mega-galleries. Rosen’s examples included Lavender Opener Chair, founded in 2020 in shared quarters with Tohmei Diner, and XYZ Collective, formed in 2011 by artists COBRA and Soshiro Matsubara and editor Madoka Hattori. Nakanishi, a co-founder of the avant-garde Hi-Red Center in the 1960s, served as a historical anchor. I had seen Rosen at Art Jakarta less than a month earlier; after Art Taipei, he was due back to Japan for Art Week Tokyo and Art Collaboration Kyoto. The self-determination he celebrates in the artist-run platforms he convened in Art Taipei found an echo in his own efforts to work differently within—not necessarily against—an unrelenting global fair circuit.

Art Taipei’s 33rd edition assembled 127 galleries, 66 from Taiwan and 61 from abroad, the highest overseas share in recent years. On the floor, offerings veered between two poles: classical, ink-inflected painting and pop-saturated, cartoon-adjacent work. The more rewarding presentations walked the line between the academic and contemporary. At the booth of Asia Art Center, a stalwart of the Taipei art scene, Dong Shaw-hwei’s multi-panel The Loquat Blooming in Courtyard (2012–21) combined flattened silhouettes and shifting vantage points, merging still life with landscape in understated olive tones. Nearby, Hong Kong artist Tobe Kiu Sin Kan’s Tangent/Rove (2025) balanced her signature cobalt blue with crisp dusk hues. The gallery brought sculptures by Taiwanese titans Ju Ming and Li Chen, and debuted works by French sculptor Bernar Venet, whose first solo show in Taiwan is currently on view at Asia Art Center.

Across the aisle, the joint booth of Tina Keng Gallery and TKG+ dispensed with regional or chronological groupings. Canvases staggered along the wall joined disparate horizon lines into a shared meditation on body, landscape, and historical memory. Another standout was Yiri Arts, a gallery that grew out of a botanical lifestyle and retail business, now with outposts in Taipei, Jakarta, and soon Guangzhou. Its quasi-retrospective presentation for Taiwan-born midcareer artist Shih Yung-Chun treated the booth as a theatrical diorama: salvaged tea caddies, mooncake tins, and childhood toys—nostalgic fixtures of the Asian household—anchored a multidisciplinary conceptual practice spanning painting, video, and installation.

SHIH YUNG-CHUN at Yiri Arts’s booth at Art Taipei 2026. Photo by and courtesy Yiri Arts.

Returning to Art Taipei after several years, Kaikai Kiki Gallery staged an immersive installation by Shoko Nakazawa. Its candy-colored kaiju , sculpted and daubed in part on-site, drew children and adults into impromptu exchanges with the artist. Across the hall, Perrotin signaled its commitment to the Taipei scene with an expansive, multi-section booth. Highlights included sculptures by Takashi Murakami, glass constellations by Jean-Michel Othoniel, and bronzes by Lynn Chadwick, a staple among Taiwan’s modern sculpture collectors. One section was devoted to new works by Chinese painter Chen Fei, whose practice has turned increasingly inward since his 2025 solo exhibition “Father and Child” at Tokyo’s Watari Museum of Contemporary Art. The display was backed by patterned wallpaper that, on closer inspection, transpired to be stylized studies of his infant daughter’s stool, scrupulously photographed day after day throughout a precarious first year of digestive complications.

In an adjoining alcove, four luminous compositions by the Iranian painter Mehdi Ghadyanloo depicted playground apparatuses, vacant slides, and carousels bathed in surreal light. Like COBRA’s game mat in “Curated Japan” and Shih’s haunted vintage toys, Ghadyanloo’s playgrounds perhaps treat play not as escapist diversion but as a kind of psychic strategy. In a market that relentlessly tests our stamina, play emerges as a disciplined way of surviving.

Michele Chan is managing editor at ArtAsiaPacific .
